page.overview:
What is Censure?

A censure is an expression of strong disapproval or harsh criticism. In parliamentary procedure, it is a debatable main motion that could be adopted by a majority vote.

Among the forms that it can take are a stern rebuke by a legislature, a spiritual penalty imposed by a church, or a negative judgement pronounced on a theological proposition.

It is usually non-binding (requiring no compulsory action from the censured party), unlike a motion of no confidence (which may require the referenced party to resign).
